items.title: Get Started with yaozarrs
items.text: Yaozarrs is a bottom-up library for working with OME-Zarr metadata and stores in Python. It is lightweight, with only a single required dependency (on Pydantic), but feature-rich, with structural validation and writing functions added via optional extras.

items.title: Quick Links
items.text:
• See installation guide for instructions on how to install yaozarrs.
  • For a quick overview of the API, see the API Quick Reference below, or the full API Reference.
  • If you're new to OME-Zarr or don't know how to express your data in OME-Zarr format, see the yaozarrs guide to OME-Zarr.
  • If you learn best with examples, check out the interactive OME-Zarr explorer app.
  • To understand why yaozarrs exists, see the Principles section below.

items.title: Metadata Creation
items.text:
You can create OME-Zarr metadata objects using the pydantic models in yaozarrs.v04, yaozarrs.v05 and yaozarrs.v06 modules. Pick a top-level object (e.g. Image, Plate, etc..) and create it using standard pydantic model syntax:

From yaozarrs modelsFrom dictionariesDimSpec Convenience

For full IDE autocompletion and type checking, you can create OME-Zarr metadata using the yaozarrs models:

v0.6v0.5 
from yaozarrs import v06

image = v06.Image(
    multiscales=[
        v06.Multiscale(
            coordinateSystems=[
                v06.CoordinateSystem(  # (1)!
                    name="physical",
                    axes=[
                        v06.TimeAxis(name="t", unit="second"),
                        v06.ChannelAxis(name="c"),
                        v06.SpaceAxis(name="z", unit="micrometer"),
                        v06.SpaceAxis(name="y", unit="micrometer"),
                        v06.SpaceAxis(name="x", unit="micrometer"),
                    ],
                )
            ],
            datasets=[
                v06.Dataset(
                    path="0",
                    coordinateTransformations=[
                        v06.ScaleTransformation(
                            scale=[1.0, 1.0, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1],
                            input={"path": "0"},  # (2)!
                            output={"name": "physical"},
                        )
                    ],
                )
            ],
        )
    ],
)

# Export
image.model_dump_json(indent=2)  # (3)!
  1. In v0.6, axes belong to a named coordinate system. See Coordinate Systems & Transformations.
  2. Each dataset's transformation says what it maps from (its array, by path) and to (a coordinate system, by name).
  3. model_dump_json is part of the standard pydantic API for exporting models to JSON. Just an example of exporting metadata back to JSON format.
from yaozarrs import v05

image = v05.Image(
    multiscales=[
        v05.Multiscale(
            name=None,
            axes=[
                v05.TimeAxis(name="t", unit="second"),
                v05.ChannelAxis(name="c"),
                v05.SpaceAxis(name="z", unit="micrometer"),
                v05.SpaceAxis(name="y", unit="micrometer"),
                v05.SpaceAxis(name="x", unit="micrometer"),
            ],
            datasets=[
                v05.Dataset(
                    path="0",
                    coordinateTransformations=[
                        v05.ScaleTransformation(scale=[1.0, 1.0, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1])
                    ],
                )
            ],
        )
    ],
)

# Export
image.model_dump_json(indent=2)  # (1)!
  1. model_dump_json is part of the standard pydantic API for exporting models to JSON. Just an example of exporting metadata back to JSON format.

If you prefer avoiding explicit model classes, you can create OME-Zarr metadata using standard python dictionaries (standard pydantic model parsing):

v0.6v0.5 
from yaozarrs import v06

image = v06.Image.model_validate(  # (1)!
    {
        "multiscales": [
            {
                "coordinateSystems": [
                    {
                        "name": "physical",
                        "axes": [
                            {"name": "t", "type": "time", "unit": "second"},
                            {"name": "c", "type": "channel"},
                            {"name": "z", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                            {"name": "y", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                            {"name": "x", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                        ],
                    }
                ],
                "datasets": [
                    {
                        "path": "0",
                        "coordinateTransformations": [
                            {
                                "type": "scale",
                                "scale": [1.0, 1.0, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1],
                                "input": {"path": "0"},
                                "output": {"name": "physical"},
                            }
                        ],
                    }
                ],
            }
        ]
    }
)

# Export
image.model_dump_json(indent=2)  # (2)!
  1. model_validate is part of the standard pydantic API for creating models from any object, like dictionaries.
  2. model_dump_json is part of the standard pydantic API for exporting models to JSON. Just an example of exporting metadata back to JSON format.
from yaozarrs import v05

image = v05.Image.model_validate(  # (1)!
    {
        "multiscales": [
            {
                "axes": [
                    {"name": "t", "type": "time", "unit": "second"},
                    {"name": "c", "type": "channel"},
                    {"name": "z", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                    {"name": "y", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                    {"name": "x", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                ],
                "datasets": [
                    {
                        "path": "0",
                        "coordinateTransformations": [
                            {"type": "scale", "scale": [1.0, 1.0, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1]}
                        ],
                    }
                ],
            }
        ]
    }
)

# Export
image.model_dump_json(indent=2)  # (2)!
  1. model_validate is part of the standard pydantic API for creating models from any object, like dictionaries.
  2. model_dump_json is part of the standard pydantic API for exporting models to JSON. Just an example of exporting metadata back to JSON format.

For the common case of creating multiscale images, you can use the yaozarrs.DimSpec convenience class to simplify axis and transformation creation. It hides the differences between versions: the same code works for v04, v05 and v06.

from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v06  # (or v04, v05)

image = v06.Image(
    multiscales=[
        v06.Multiscale.from_dims(
            dims=[
                DimSpec(name="t", unit="second"),  # (1)!
                DimSpec(name="c"),
                DimSpec(name="z", scale=0.3, unit="micrometer"),
                DimSpec(name="y", scale=0.1, unit="micrometer"),
                DimSpec(name="x", scale=0.1, unit="micrometer"),
            ]
        )
    ]
)

# Export
image.model_dump_json(indent=2)  # (2)!
  1. yaozarrs.DimSpec is a convenience class for use with Multiscale.from_dims. It's not part of the OME-Zarr spec.
  2. model_dump_json is part of the standard pydantic API for exporting models to JSON. Just an example of exporting metadata back to JSON format.

items.title: Validation of existing objects
items.text:
If you have an existing JSON file, string, or python object, you can validate it and cast it to the appropriate typed yaozarrs model:

import yaozarrs

# validate a JSON string/bytes literal
yaozarrs.validate_ome_json(json_str)  # (1)!

# validate any python object (e.g. dict)
yaozarrs.validate_ome_object(dict_obj)  # (2)!

# validate entire Zarr hierarchy (both metadata and structure) at any URI
yaozarrs.validate_zarr_store(uri)  # (3)!
  1. yaozarrs.validate_ome_json
  2. yaozarrs.validate_ome_object
  3. yaozarrs.validate_zarr_store. Requires the yaozarrs[io] extra to support remote URIs.
Keys the spec doesn't define

The spec doesn't forbid keys it doesn't define, and neither do the JSON schemas (except in the input and output of v0.6 scene transformations), so yaozarrs keeps them: they're in each model's model_extra, and model_dump() / model_dump_json() write them back out. So a misspelled optional key is (unfortunately) kept as an unknown key, not reported.

Storage Validation Errors

Validation errors that relate to the structure of the OME-Zarr itself (as opposed to metadata) are collected and presented similarly to pydantic validation errors for the metadata:

items.title: Doing the IO yourself
items.text:
Validation never reads array data, and only the parts that compare documents need to read anything at all:

What is validated How IO Fields, and the consistency of one document validate_ome_json, validate_ome_object, or the models directly None: you pass in the document Consistency across a hierarchy of documents validate_zarr_store Metadata only: fsspec, or a mapping that you provide Values stored in arrays (e.g. the orthonormality of a rotation stored at a path) Not validated

validate_zarr_store and open_group accept any Mapping[str, bytes] of store keys to metadata documents, so you decide how those documents are fetched. A custom mapping can fetch them lazily in __getitem__, or you can fetch them up front and pass a dict:

import json
import yaozarrs

image_meta = {
    "version": "0.5",
    "multiscales": [
        {
            "axes": [
                {"name": "y", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
                {"name": "x", "type": "space", "unit": "micrometer"},
            ],
            "datasets": [
                {
                    "path": "0",
                    "coordinateTransformations": [
                        {"type": "scale", "scale": [1.0, 1.0]}
                    ],
                }
            ],
        }
    ],
}
group = {"zarr_format": 3, "node_type": "group", "attributes": {"ome": image_meta}}
array = {
    "zarr_format": 3,
    "node_type": "array",
    "shape": [64, 64],
    "data_type": "uint8",
    "chunk_grid": {"name": "regular", "configuration": {"chunk_shape": [64, 64]}},
    "chunk_key_encoding": {"name": "default"},
    "fill_value": 0,
    "codecs": [{"name": "bytes"}],
    "dimension_names": ["y", "x"],
}

store = {
    f"{path}zarr.json": json.dumps(doc).encode()
    for path, doc in [("", group), ("0/", array)]
}
yaozarrs.validate_zarr_store(store)

Note

Anything that needs a URI (store_path, to_zarr_python() and to_tensorstore()) raises a TypeError for these stores.

items.title: Writing OME-Zarr Stores
items.text:
See Writing OME-Zarr for functions to write OME-Zarr v0.5 and v0.6 stores from your metadata objects, with either zarr-python, tensorstore, or custom backends.

import numpy as np

from yaozarrs import write

# write a 5D image with single pyramid level
data = np.zeros((10, 3, 9, 64, 64), dtype=np.uint16)
root_path = write.v06.write_image("example.ome.zarr", image, data)

# other high level write functions
write.v06.write_plate(...)
write.v06.write_bioformats2raw(...)
write.v06.write_scene(...)  # v0.6 only

# low-level prepare/builder functions
write.v06.prepare_image(...)
write.v06.LabelsBuilder(...)
write.v06.PlateBuilder(...)
write.v06.Bf2RawBuilder(...)
write.v06.SceneBuilder(...)  # v0.6 only

# write.v05 has the same functions (for v05 models), except for scenes

items.title: CLI validation
items.text:
The CLI command provides a quick way to validate any zarr store as an OME-Zarr store. Here, "store" refers to any URI (local path, http(s) url, or s3 url.

Important

Requires fsspec. install with pip install yaozarrs[io]

with uvxfrom installed package 
uvx "yaozarrs[io]" validate https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imaging-formats/yaozarrs/refs/heads/main/tests/data/broken/broken_v05.ome.zarr/

yaozarrs validate https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imaging-formats/yaozarrs/refs/heads/main/tests/data/broken/broken_v05.ome.zarr/

✓ Valid OME-Zarr store
  Version: 0.5
  Type: Image

items.title: CLI tree view
items.text:
Visualize the hierarchy of any OME-Zarr store with yaozarrs tree:

with uvxfrom installed package 
uvx "yaozarrs[io]" tree https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr

yaozarrs tree https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr

🖼️ 6001240_labels.zarr
├── zarr.json  <- v05.Image
├── 📦 0 (uint16, (2, 236, 275, 271))
├── 📦 1 (uint16, (2, 236, 137, 135))
├── 📦 2 (uint16, (2, 236, 68, 67))
└── 🏷️ labels
    ├── zarr.json  <- v05.LabelsGroup
    └── 🖼️ 0
        ├── zarr.json  <- v05.LabelImage
        ├── 📦 0 (int8, (1, 236, 275, 271))
        ├── 📦 1 (int8, (1, 236, 137, 135))
        ├── 📦 2 (int8, (1, 236, 68, 67))
        └── 📦 3 (int8, (1, 236, 34, 33))

Use --depth / -d to limit traversal depth, and --max-per-level / -n to cap the number of children shown at each level.

items.title: Loading OME-Zarr Stores
items.text:
yaozarrs.open_group returns a small wrapper around a zarr group with minimal functionality: yaozarrs.ZarrGroup. Requires the yaozarrs[io] extra to support remote URIs. This class is used behind the scenes for structural validation, but can also be used directly.

import yaozarrs

# Open a Zarr group at any URI
group = yaozarrs.open_group(uri)
print(group.ome_metadata())  # (1)!
child = group["0"]  # (2)!
  1. ZarrGroup.ome_metadata attempts to extract and validate OME-Zarr metadata from the opened group, returning the appropriate typed yaozarrs model (e.g. yaozarrs.v05.Image, etc..).
  2. Access arrays and sub-groups using standard dictionary-like syntax. Returns ZarrArray or ZarrGroup

You can also get a tree view of the hierarchy programmatically with ZarrGroup.tree():

print(group.tree(depth=2))

items.title: Access array data
items.text:
This package does not depend on zarr or tensorstore, even for validating OME-Zarr stores. (It uses a minimal representation of a zarr group internally, backed by fsspec.) If you would like to actually open arrays, you can use either ZarrArray.to_tensorstore or ZarrArray.to_zarr_python to cast an array node to a full zarr array using your preferred backend.

Important

These methods require that you have the appropriate backend installed (tensorstore or zarr).

from yaozarrs import open_group

group = open_group(
    "https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr"
)
array = group["0"]
# <ZarrArray https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr/0>

# read bytes using tensorstore or zarr-python:
ts_array = array.to_tensorstore()  # isinstance(ts_array, tensorstore.TensorStore)
zarr_array = array.to_zarr_python()  # isinstance(zarr_array, zarr.Array)

items.title: Principles
items.text:
The core philosophy is that NGFF metadata and Zarr array I/O are separate concerns.

Yaozarrs focuses on OME-Zarr metadata creation, manipulation, and validation, and all other functionality (writing and structural validation) is optional, with flexible backend.

Zarr itself is a specification with multiple implementations: There are many ways to read and write Zarr stores (e.g. zarr-python, tensorstore, acquire-zarr, zarrs, etc..) and yaozarrs makes no assumptions about which implementation you may want to use. Similarly, OME NGFF is a metadata specification, defining what JSON documents and hierarchy structure must look like.

  1. At its core, yaozarrs provides pydantic models for OME-Zarr metadata specifications. You should be able to create/manipulate/validate OME-Zarr metadata without any specific zarr array library, or anything beyond yaozarrs, pydantic, and the standard library.

    Why pydantic?

    It's true that one can define dataclasses that mirror the OME-Zarr schema; but reinventing validation and ser/deserialization is beyond the scope of this project, and pydantic is a battle-tested library for exactly these tasks. It's lightweight in terms of transitive dependencies, ~7MB in size, and is broadly compatible. We test against a broad range of pydantic versions (v2+) on a broad range of python versions and OS, to ensure that yaozarrs is an easy/robust dependency to add.

  2. Because reading/writing zarr groups is far simpler than arrays, you shouldn't need to depend on a specific complete zarr library just to validate that a given hierarchy is structurally correct. For example: a library implementing a new low-level zarr array backend should be able to use yaozarrs to validate that its group structure and metadata are correct, without needing to depend on zarr-python or tensorstore.

    pip install 'yaozarrs[io]'

    If you want to perform structural validation of possibly remote zarr stores, then you will need to install the io extra, which adds dependencies on fsspec.

  3. Even in the case of writing complete OME-Zarr stores, the "array" part is relatively stereotyped, and the metadata is the more user-customized part. With yaozarrs, you can create the metadata using the pydantic models, and then use convenience functions to write the zarr stores using any zarr array creation method you want, with built-in (optional) implementations for zarr-python and tensorstore.

    pip install 'yaozarrs[write-zarr]' or [write-tensorstore]

    The builtin backends in the yaozarrs.write module require an array-writing backend, currently either zarr (zarr-python) or tensorstore. Install the appropriate extra to enable these features.

items.title: See Also
items.text:
ome-zarr-models-py is another set of Pydantic models for OME-Zarr. It has garnered broad community support, and aligns well with many use cases. It should also be considered for OME-Zarr metadata validation and manipulation in Python!

The primary difference is that it depends on zarr-python, and is more directly tied to the zarr-python implementation.

items.title: Installing yaozarrs
items.text:
The basic package (with no extras) supports metadata creation & validation, but lacks structural validation and writing capabilities.

from PyPI, with pipfrom PyPI, with uvfrom githubfrom conda 
pip install yaozarrs

uv add yaozarrs

To install the bleeding-edge development version from GitHub, (shown here using the io extra as an example):

pip install "yaozarrs[io] @ git+https://github.com/imaging-formats/yaozarrs.git"

conda install conda-forge::yaozarrs

Note that the conda distribution contains only the core package and no extras. You will need to manually install the following dependencies if you need them:

  • conda-forge::fsspec - for yaozarrs.open_group and any structural validation.
  • conda-forge::zarr OR conda-forge::tensorstore - for writing support.

items.title: Structural validation
items.text:
To enable validation of Zarr hierarchies, include the io extra when installing. This brings in fsspec (but not zarr-python):

with pipwith uv 
pip install "yaozarrs[io]"

uv add "yaozarrs[io]"

items.title: Writing support
items.text: If you want to use the convenience functions in yaozarrs.write, to create complete OME-Zarr stores with array data, you will need to pick a zarr-array library:

items.title: zarr-python
items.text:
zarr-python is the reference implementation of the Zarr specification for Python.

with pipwith uv 
pip install "yaozarrs[write-zarr]"

uv add "yaozarrs[write-zarr]"

Then use writer="zarr" in the yaozarrs.write functions.

items.title: tensorstore
items.text:
Tensorstore is an alternative zarr-array library developed by Google, which can offer better I/O performance in most cases.

with pipwith uv 
pip install "yaozarrs[write-tensorstore]"

uv add "yaozarrs[write-tensorstore]"

Then use writer="tensorstore" in the yaozarrs.write functions.

items.title: Custom backend
items.text: If you don't want to use either of the provided backends, you can implement your own array-writing functionality

items.title: OME-Zarr Explorer
items.text:
What is this?

This educational app demonstrates how various OME-NGFF zarr hierarchies are structured, along with associated metadata.

  • Define your image dimensions and view the generated hierarchy and metadata in real-time.
  • The file tree on the left demonstrates what the OME-Zarr hierarchy would look like when saved to disk
  • The Spec JSON tab shows the metadata associated with each group or array
  • The Python tab shows how you would create the metadata programmatically using the yaozarrs library.

This is meant for educational purposes only and is not intended for production use.

items.title: Writing OME-Zarr
items.text:
yaozarrs.write.v05 and yaozarrs.write.v06 write complete OME-Zarr stores (metadata and array data) to a local directory. They have the same functions: use the one that matches the version of your metadata models. v0.6 adds write_scene and SceneBuilder, for scenes.

Writing needs an array backend, see Array writer backends.

items.title: The general pattern
items.text:
1. Build the metadata model that matches your data (see the Guide to OME-Zarr): an Image, a Plate, a Bf2Raw collection, or (v0.6) a Scene.
  2. Pick a high level write_* function, or a lower level builder.
  3. Call it with your model and your data.

Each Dataset (resolution level) in an image's multiscale becomes one array in the store, so functions that take arrays (or (shape, dtype) pairs) expect one per dataset, in the same order.

import numpy as np

from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v06
from yaozarrs.write.v06 import prepare_image, write_image

dims = [
    DimSpec(name="y", scale=0.1, unit="micrometer"),
    DimSpec(name="x", scale=0.1, unit="micrometer"),
]
image = v06.Image(multiscales=[v06.Multiscale.from_dims(dims)])
data = np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint16)

# all at once
write_image("image.ome.zarr", image, data)

# or: create the hierarchy with empty arrays, and fill them yourself
path, arrays = prepare_image("prepared.ome.zarr", image, (data.shape, data.dtype))
arrays["0"][:] = data

items.title: High level functions
items.text:
These take all the data at once, write it, and return the Path to the root of the store.

Function Writes write_image an image (with optional labels) v0.5 · v0.6 write_plate a multi-well plate v0.5 · v0.6 write_bioformats2raw a bioformats2raw collection v0.5 · v0.6 write_scene a scene of images v0.6

items.title: Builders
items.text:
When you don't have all the data up front, or want more control over how it's written, the lower level functions prepare the hierarchy: they write the metadata, create empty arrays, and give them back to you (keyed by path) to fill however you like (chunk by chunk, in parallel, ...).

Function Prepares prepare_image an image v0.5 · v0.6 LabelsBuilder the label images of an image v0.5 · v0.6 PlateBuilder a multi-well plate v0.5 · v0.6 Bf2RawBuilder a bioformats2raw collection v0.5 · v0.6 SceneBuilder a scene of images v0.6

The builders can be used in two ways:

  • incremental: write one well, label or image at a time (e.g. PlateBuilder.write_well()), and the parent metadata is updated after each one.
  • prepare-only: register everything with add_*(), then prepare() creates the whole hierarchy with empty arrays.

For plates and bioformats2raw collections, the builders are usually the easier choice.

items.title: Array writer backends
items.text:
Every function takes a writer argument, which picks the library that creates the arrays:

  • "zarr": zarr-python, pip install "yaozarrs[write-zarr]"
  • "tensorstore": tensorstore, pip install "yaozarrs[write-tensorstore]"
  • "auto" (the default): tensorstore if it's installed, zarr-python otherwise
  • your own function, see Custom writers

items.title: DimSpec
items.text:
Bases: _BaseModel

Specification for a single dimension of an OME-Zarr image.

Warning

This is a convenience class and is not a part of the OME-Zarr specification.

There are some places in the OME Zarr spec where information about a given axis must be entered in multiple different places (e.g., Multiscale.axes must agree with Multiscale.datasets.CoordinateTransformation, etc). DimSpec is a convenience class that encapsulates all the relevant information about a single dimension in one place, and may be used in specialized constructors (e.g. v05.Multiscale.from_dims)

Examples:

5D timelapse with channels:

from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v05

dims = [
    DimSpec(name="t", size=100, scale=1.0, unit="second"),
    DimSpec(name="c", size=3),
    DimSpec(name="z", size=50, scale=2.0, unit="micrometer"),
    DimSpec(name="y", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    DimSpec(name="x", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
]
multiscale = v05.Multiscale.from_dims(dims, name="my_image", n_levels=3)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

The name of the dimension. Common names like 'x', 'y', 'z' will be inferred as spatial dimensions; 't' as time; 'c' as channel.

required size int | None

The size of the dimension (number of elements along this axis). This is not used anywhere by the OME-Zarr spec, but is useful when creating new empty datasets.

None scale float

The scale factor for this dimension in physical units.

1.0 unit str | None

The physical unit for this dimension (e.g., 'micrometer', 'second'). If not provided, no unit will be set on the axis.

None type Literal['space', 'time', 'channel'] | str | None

The type of axis ('space', 'time', 'channel', or custom). If not provided, will be inferred from the name: x/y/z -> 'space', t -> 'time', c -> 'channel'.

None scale_factor float | None

The scale factor for downsampling along this dimension at each multiscale level. If not provided, defaults to 2.0 for spatial dimensions (x/y/z) and 1.0 for others. To avoid downsampling along the z dimension (which is inferred to be a spatial dimension), set this explicitly to 1.0.

None translation float | None

The translation offset for this dimension in physical units. If not provided, no translation transform will be applied. If only some dimensions have translation specified, all others will default to 0.0.

None

infer_scale_factor() -> float

Infer the scale factor for downsampling based on dimension type.

Magic Alert

By default, this downscales all spatial dimensions by 2 when creating pyramid levels. Explicitly set scale_factor to override.

Source code in src/yaozarrs/_dim_spec.py 
def infer_scale_factor(self) -> float:
    """Infer the scale factor for downsampling based on dimension type.

    !!! warning ":sparkles:{ .pulse } **Magic Alert** "
        *By default, this downscales all spatial dimensions by 2 when creating
        pyramid levels.  Explicitly set `scale_factor` to override.*

    """
    if self.scale_factor is not None:
        return self.scale_factor
    return 2.0 if self.infer_type() == "space" else 1.0

Infer the axis type from the dimension name.

Magic Alert

This treats names of "x", "y", "z", "t", "time", "c", and "channel" specially!

Returns:

Type Description str | None

Source code in src/yaozarrs/_dim_spec.py 
def infer_type(self) -> str | None:
    """Infer the axis type from the dimension name.

    !!! warning ":sparkles:{ .pulse } **Magic Alert** "
        *This treats names of "x", "y", "z", "t", "time", "c", and "channel"
        specially!*

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The inferred type: 'space' for x/y/z, 'time' for t, 'channel' for c,
        or the explicitly set type if provided.
    """
    if self.type is not None:
        return self.type
    name_lower = self.name.lower()
    if name_lower in ("x", "y", "z"):
        return "space"
    if name_lower in {"t", "time"}:
        return "time"
    if name_lower in {"c", "channel"}:
        return "channel"
    return None

def get_details(

    *,
    include_context: bool = True,
) -> list[ErrorDetails]:
    """
    Details about each validation issue.

    Parameters
    ----------
    include_context: bool
        Whether to include the context of each item.

    Returns
    -------
        A list of `ErrorDetails` for each validation issue.
    """
    filtered_details: list[ErrorDetails] = []
    for detail in self._details:
        filtered_detail: ErrorDetails = {
            "type": detail["type"],
            "loc": detail["loc"],
            "msg": detail["msg"],
        }
        if include_context and "ctx" in detail:
            filtered_detail["ctx"] = detail["ctx"]
        filtered_details.append(filtered_detail)
    return filtered_details

Minimal wrapper around a zarr v2/v3 group.

Important

Requires yaozarrs[io] or fsspec to be installed, unless the store is a mapping that you provide yourself (see yaozarrs.open_group).

This class exists to provide minimal zarr group functionality, needed for hierarchy traversal and structural validation, without requiring a dependency on a full blown zarr array-writing library (which come with heavier dependencies, and python version limitations).

Matches zarr-python behavior: expects all children to be the same zarr_format version as the parent. Does not support mixed hierarchies.

def __init__(
    self,
    store: Mapping[str, bytes],
    path: str = "",
    meta: ZarrMetadata | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize a zarr node.

    Parameters
    ----------
    store : Mapping[str, bytes]
        The mapping for the zarr store (e.g. an FSMap, or a dict).  Anything other
        than a _CachedMapper will be wrapped in one, for performance.
    path : str
        The path to this node within the zarr store (relative to the store root).
    meta : dict[str, Any] | ZarrMetadata | None
        Optional pre-loaded metadata dictionary. If not provided, it will be
        loaded from the store.
    """
    # Ensure we have a cached mapper for performance
    if not isinstance(store, _CachedMapper):
        store = _CachedMapper(store)

    self._store = store
    self._path = str(path).rstrip("/")
    if meta is None:
        self._metadata = _load_zarr_metadata(self._store, self._path)
    elif isinstance(meta, ZarrMetadata):
        if meta.node_type != self.node_type():  # pragma: no cover
            raise ValueError(
                f"Metadata node_type '{meta.node_type}' does not match "
                f"expected '{self.node_type()}'"
            )
        self._metadata = meta
    else:  # pragma: no cover
        raise ValueError("meta must be a ZarrMetadata instance or None")

def ome_version(self) -> str | None:
    """Return ome_version if present, else None.

    Attempt to determine version as minimally as possible without
    parsing full models. For bioformats2raw layouts, looks into child "0".
    """
    if v := self._local_ome_version():
        return v
    # special case for bioformats2raw layouts...
    # which, prior to v0.5, may not have version in the attrs, and may have no
    # other indication of version except in child "0".
    if "bioformats2raw.layout" in self._metadata.attributes:
        if "0" in self and isinstance(group := self["0"], ZarrGroup):
            return group.ome_version()
    return None

def validate(self, *, strict: bool | None = None) -> Self:
    """Validate the zarr group structure.

    This is a convenience method that calls [`yaozarrs.validate_zarr_store`][]
    on this group.

    Parameters
    ----------
    strict : bool | None
        If `True`, reject input that would otherwise be coerced to the right type
        (e.g. `"1"` for an integer). By default, such input is accepted.

    Raises
    ------
    StorageValidationError
        If the storage structure is invalid.
    """
    from yaozarrs._validate import validate_zarr_store

    validate_zarr_store(self, strict=strict)
    return self

def tree(
    self, *, depth: int | None = None, max_per_level: int | None = None
) -> str:
    """Return a tree representation of the zarr group hierarchy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    depth : int | None, optional
        Maximum depth to traverse. None for unlimited depth.
        Using a smaller depth improves performance for large hierarchies.
    max_per_level : int | None, optional
        Maximum number of children to show at each level.
        Additional children are indicated with an ellipsis.
        None for unlimited children.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        String representation of the tree.

    Notes
    -----
    Uses rich library for enhanced rendering if available,
    otherwise falls back to plain text with Unicode box characters.

    Icons:
    - 📦 Array nodes
    - 🖼️ Image groups (multiscales)
    - 🏷️ Label image groups
    - 🅾️ Other OME-zarr group nodes
    - 📁 Regular group nodes
    - ⋯  Indicates truncated children (when max_per_level is exceeded)

    Examples
    --------
    >>> url = "https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr"
    >>> group = open_group(url)
    >>> print(group.tree(depth=2, max_per_level=5))
    🖼️ 6001240_labels.zarr
    ├── zarr.json  <- v05.Image
    ├── 📦 0 (uint16, (2, 236, 275, 271))
    ├── 📦 1 (uint16, (2, 236, 137, 135))
    ├── 📦 2 (uint16, (2, 236, 68, 67))

        ├── zarr.json  <- v05.LabelsGroup
        └── 🖼️ 0

def ome_metadata(
    self, *, version: str | None = None, strict: bool | None = None
) -> v06.OMEMetadata | v05.OMEMetadata | v04.OMEZarrGroupJSON | None:
    """Return the OME metadata (as a yaozarrs object) if present, else None.

    Parameters
    ----------
    version : str | None
        Optional OME-Zarr version to use when parsing metadata.
        If not provided (default), will attempt to infer from local or inherited
        attrs.  This determines the union of types that will be tried when casting
        metadata to a yaozarrs model.
    strict : bool | None
        If `True`, reject input that would otherwise be coerced to the right type
        (e.g. `"1"` for an integer). By default, such input is accepted.

    Returns
    -------
    BaseModel | None
        A yaozarrs OME metadata model (v0.4, v0.5 or v0.6) if found, else None.
    """
    if strict or not hasattr(self, "_ome_metadata"):
        meta = self._metadata
        fallback_version = (
            version or self._local_ome_version() or self._inherited_ome_version()
        )
        result = meta.ome_metadata(version=fallback_version, strict=strict)
        if strict:  # the cache holds the default (coercing) result
            return result
        self._ome_metadata = result
    return self._ome_metadata

Prefetch metadata for multiple children using async batch fetching.

For HTTPS URIs, this triggers fsspec's async batch fetching which uses aiohttp to fetch up to 1280 files concurrently. Results are cached in the _CachedMapper for subsequent access.

This is critical for performance with remote stores - a 384-well plate can have 2000+ metadata files. Without batching, sequential fetches would take 10+ minutes; with batching, validation completes in ~80 seconds.

Name Type Description Default child_keys list[str]

def prefetch_children(self, child_keys: Iterable[str]) -> None:
    """Prefetch metadata for multiple children using async batch fetching.

    For HTTPS URIs, this triggers fsspec's async batch fetching which uses
    aiohttp to fetch up to 1280 files concurrently. Results are cached in
    the _CachedMapper for subsequent access.

    This is critical for performance with remote stores - a 384-well plate
    can have 2000+ metadata files. Without batching, sequential fetches would
    take 10+ minutes; with batching, validation completes in ~80 seconds.

    Parameters
    ----------
    child_keys : list[str]
        List of child keys to prefetch.
    """
    # Build list of metadata file paths to fetch
    metadata_paths = []
    for key in child_keys:
        child_path = f"{self._path}/{key}" if self._path else key
        if self._metadata.zarr_format >= 3:
            metadata_paths.append(f"{child_path}/zarr.json")
        else:
            # For v2, we need to check .zgroup, .zarray, AND .zattrs
            # The .zattrs file contains OME metadata and must be prefetched
            # to avoid individual HTTP requests when loading group metadata
            metadata_paths.extend(
                [
                    f"{child_path}/.zgroup",
                    f"{child_path}/.zarray",
                    f"{child_path}/.zattrs",
                ]
            )

    # Batch fetch using getitems - _CachedMapper handles fallback if needed
    try:
        self._store.getitems(metadata_paths)
    except Exception:
        # If batch fetching fails, _CachedMapper will fall back to sequential
        # access when files are actually requested via __getitem__
        pass

def __contains__(self, key: str) -> bool:
    """Check if a child node exists."""
    child_path = f"{self._path}/{key}" if self._path else key

    if self._metadata.zarr_format >= 3:
        return f"{child_path}/zarr.json" in self._store
    else:
        return (

            or f"{child_path}/.zarray" in self._store

Only metadata is converted: no store is read or written, and arrays are not touched. (Note that v0.4 stores use Zarr v2, while later versions use Zarr v3.)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default obj Any

The model to convert: an Image, LabelImage, LabelsGroup, Plate, Well, Bf2Raw, Series, Multiscale or Scene of any version, or an OMEZarrGroupJSON or OMEAttributes. It is not modified.

required version '0.4' | '0.5' | '0.6'

The version to convert to. Converting to the same version returns a new, revalidated model (and normalizes a pre-release version like "0.6.dev4").

required coordinate_system str

Name for the intrinsic coordinate system, when converting to v0.6 from an older version. An existing coordinate system is never renamed. Default is "intrinsic". (Older versions have no coordinate systems, so converting from v0.6 doesn't keep its name: pass it here to restore it.)

'intrinsic'

Returns:

Type Description Any

The same kind of model, in the target version. v0.4 has no OMEZarrGroupJSON or OMEAttributes model, so those convert to the metadata document they hold.

Warns:

Type Description ConversionWarning

If the target version can't express some of the metadata, which is dropped. Use warnings.filterwarnings("error", category=ConversionWarning) to raise instead.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If obj is not a model that can be converted.

ValueError

If version is unknown, or has no equivalent of obj (e.g. a v0.6 Scene).

ValidationError

If the metadata is not valid in the target version (e.g. 6 axes in v0.5).

Examples:

>>> from yaozarrs import DimSpec, convert_version, v04
>>> dims = [DimSpec(name="y", size=64), DimSpec(name="x", size=64)]
>>> image = v04.Image(multiscales=[v04.Multiscale.from_dims(dims)])
>>> convert_version(image, "0.6").version

Source code in src/yaozarrs/_convert.py 
def convert_version(
    obj: Any,
    version: Literal["0.4", "0.5", "0.6"],
    *,
    coordinate_system: str = "intrinsic",
) -> Any:
    """Convert an OME-Zarr metadata model to another version of the spec.

    Only metadata is converted: no store is read or written, and arrays are not
    touched.  (Note that v0.4 stores use Zarr v2, while later versions use Zarr v3.)

    Parameters
    ----------
    obj : Any
        The model to convert: an `Image`, `LabelImage`, `LabelsGroup`, `Plate`, `Well`,
        `Bf2Raw`, `Series`, `Multiscale` or `Scene` of any version, or an
        `OMEZarrGroupJSON` or `OMEAttributes`. It is not modified.
    version : "0.4" | "0.5" | "0.6"
        The version to convert to.  Converting to the same version returns a new,
        revalidated model (and normalizes a pre-release `version` like "0.6.dev4").
    coordinate_system : str, optional
        Name for the intrinsic coordinate system, when converting to v0.6 from an
        older version.  An existing coordinate system is never renamed.
        Default is "intrinsic".  (Older versions have no coordinate systems, so
        converting from v0.6 doesn't keep its name: pass it here to restore it.)

    Returns
    -------
    Any
        The same kind of model, in the target version.  v0.4 has no `OMEZarrGroupJSON`
        or `OMEAttributes` model, so those convert to the metadata document they hold.

    Warns
    -----
    ConversionWarning
        If the target version can't express some of the metadata, which is dropped.
        Use `warnings.filterwarnings("error", category=ConversionWarning)` to raise
        instead.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `obj` is not a model that can be converted.
    ValueError
        If `version` is unknown, or has no equivalent of `obj` (e.g. a v0.6 `Scene`).
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If the metadata is not valid in the target version (e.g. 6 axes in v0.5).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from yaozarrs import DimSpec, convert_version, v04
    >>> dims = [DimSpec(name="y", size=64), DimSpec(name="x", size=64)]
    >>> image = v04.Image(multiscales=[v04.Multiscale.from_dims(dims)])
    >>> convert_version(image, "0.6").version
    '0.6'
    """
    if version not in _PACKAGES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown version {version!r}, expected one of {_ORDER}.")

    dropped: list[str] = []
    result = _convert(obj, version, coordinate_system, dropped)
    if dropped:
        warnings.warn(
            f"Converting to OME-Zarr v{version} dropped metadata that it can't "
            f"express: {', '.join(dict.fromkeys(dropped))}.",
            ConversionWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return result

May also be any mapping of store keys to the bytes of the metadata documents (e.g. {"zarr.json": b"...", "0/zarr.json": b"..."}). Only metadata keys are read, and a missing key must behave as it does for a dict: get returns None.

def open_group(
    uri: str | os.PathLike | Mapping[str, bytes] | Any,
    storage_options: dict | None = None,
) -> ZarrGroup:
    """Open a zarr v2/v3 group from a URI or a mapping.

    !!!important
        Requires `yaozarrs[io]` or `fsspec` to be installed, unless `uri` is a mapping.

    Returns a small wrapper around the zarr group that allows reading metadata and
    traversing the hierarchy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uri : str | os.PathLike | Mapping[str, bytes]
        The URI of the zarr store (e.g., "https://...", "s3://...", "/path/to/file"),
        or a zarr-python Group.  May also be any mapping of store keys to the bytes of
        the metadata documents (e.g. `{"zarr.json": b"...", "0/zarr.json": b"..."}`).
        Only metadata keys are read, and a missing key must behave as it does for a
        dict: `get` returns `None`.
    storage_options : dict | None
        Additional storage options to pass to fsspec when opening the mapper.
        Ignored if `uri` is a mapping.

    Returns
    -------
    ZarrGroup
        The opened zarr group with caching enabled.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If no zarr metadata is found at the specified URI.
    ValueError
        If the metadata is invalid or inconsistent, or if the root node is not a group.
    """
    if isinstance(uri, ZarrGroup):
        return uri

    # (zarr-python v2 Groups are mappings too, but of nodes, not bytes: handled below)
    if isinstance(uri, Mapping) and not _is_zarr_python(uri):
        return _open_group_at(uri)

    try:
        from fsspec import FSMap, get_mapper
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(
            "fsspec package is required for open_group() with a URI.  "
            "Please install with `pip install yaozarrs[io]` or "
            "`pip install fsspec`."
        ) from e

    if isinstance(uri, (str, os.PathLike)):
        uri = os.path.expanduser(os.fspath(uri))
    elif hasattr(uri, "store"):
        # Handle both zarr v2 and v3 Group objects
        # v3: str(group.store) returns a URI like "file:///path"
        # v2: group.store.path returns the directory path
        if hasattr(uri.store, "path"):
            # Zarr v2: DirectoryStore has .path attribute
            uri = uri.store.path
        else:
            # Zarr v3: LocalStore's __str__ returns URI
            uri = str(uri.store)
    else:  # pragma: no cover
        raise TypeError(
            "uri must be a string, os.PathLike, a mapping, or have a 'store' attribute"
        )

    storage_options = storage_options or {}
    if str(uri).startswith("s3://"):
        storage_options.setdefault("anon", True)
    elif str(uri).startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        # Without a timeout, a hung connection can stall validation
        # indefinitely (aiohttp's own default is a 5-minute total timeout,
        # and batch fetches may queue hundreds of requests behind it).
        import aiohttp

        client_kwargs = storage_options.setdefault("client_kwargs", {})
        client_kwargs.setdefault("timeout", aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30))
    mapper = get_mapper(uri, **storage_options)

    if not isinstance(mapper, FSMap):  # pragma: no cover
        raise TypeError(f"Expected FSMap from get_mapper, got {type(mapper)}")

    return _open_group_at(mapper)

def validate_ome_json(
    data: str | bytes | bytearray,
    cls: type[T] | Any = None,
    *,
    strict: bool | None = None,
) -> T | AnyOME:
    """Validate any ome-zarr JSON string or bytes literal.

    By default, this will validate `data` against all known OME JSON documents.
    This includes ome-zarr group documents for v04 (found at .zattrs in the zarr group)
    and v05/v06 (found at zarr.json in the zarr group).  For v05 and v06 objects, it
    also detects data that would be valid as the value of the
    `data["attributes"]["ome"]` key inside a zarr.json document.  A v0.5 or v0.6
    document must declare its `version`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : str | bytes | bytearray
        The OMENode instance to validate.
    cls : type[T]
        The class to validate against. Must be a subclass of `BaseModel`.
        If not provided, defaults to `OMENode`, meaning any valid OME node object
    strict : bool | None
        If `True`, reject input that would otherwise be coerced to the right type
        (e.g. `"1"` for an integer). By default, such input is accepted.

    Returns
    -------
    object: T
        The validated (pydantic) model instance.

    Raises
    ------
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If the validation fails.
    """
    if cls is not None and cls is not _AnyOMEGroupByVersion:
        return type_adapter(cls).validate_json(data, strict=strict)
    adapter: TypeAdapter[AnyOME] = type_adapter(cls or _AnyOMEByVersion)
    try:
        return adapter.validate_json(data, strict=strict)
    except ValidationError:
        try:
            error = _version_error(json.loads(data))
        except ValueError:  # (not JSON)
            error = None
        if error:
            raise error from None
        raise

def validate_ome_uri(
    uri: str | os.PathLike, cls: type[T] | Any = None, *, strict: bool | None = None
) -> T | AnyOMEGroup:
    """Load and validate root metadata in a OME-Zarr group from a URI or local path.

    !!!important
        This requires that you have installed yaozarrs with the `io` extra, e.g.
        `pip install yaozarrs[io]`.

    This function will attempt to load the OME-Zarr group metadata from the given URI or
    local path. The URI should be a path to a zarr group (directory or URL) with valid
    ome-zarr metadata, or a path directly to the metadata JSON file itself (e.g.
    zarr.json or .zattrs).

    **This _only_ loads and validates the root OME-Zarr group metadata.**  It does not
    traverse the hierarchy, perform structural validation, or validate any child groups
    or arrays.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uri : str | os.PathLike
        The URI or local path to the OME-Zarr group. This can be a file path,
        a directory path, or a URL.
    cls : type[T]
        The class to validate against. Must be a subclass of `BaseModel`.
    strict : bool | None
        If `True`, reject input that would otherwise be coerced to the right type
        (e.g. `"1"` for an integer). By default, such input is accepted.

    Returns
    -------
    AnyOME: T
        An instance of `v06.OMEZarrGroupJSON`, `v05.OMEZarrGroupJSON`,
        `v04.OMEZarrGroupJSON`, or another valid OME-Zarr node type, depending on the
        object detected.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If the URI does not point to a valid OME-Zarr group.
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If the loaded metadata is not valid according to the OME-Zarr specification.
    """
    from ._io import read_json_from_uri

    json_content, uri_str = read_json_from_uri(uri)
    cls = cls or _AnyOMEGroupByVersion
    obj = validate_ome_json(json_content, cls, strict=strict)  # type: ignore
    obj.uri = uri_str
    return obj

Important

This is a high-level function to validate both the metadata and the structure of a complete OME-Zarr store. This is the function used by the yaozarrs validate CLI command.

Supports OME-Zarr versions 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6.

Can be a URI string, a Path, a ZarrGroup instance, a zarr.Group object (for backwards compatibility), or a mapping of store keys to the bytes of the metadata documents, if you want to do the IO yourself (see yaozarrs.open_group). To validate a single document without a store, use yaozarrs.validate_ome_object or yaozarrs.validate_ome_json.

def validate_zarr_store(
    obj: ZarrGroup | str | Path | Mapping[str, bytes] | Any,
    *,
    strict: bool | None = None,
) -> ZarrGroup:
    """Validate both structure and metadata of an OME-Zarr hierarchy.

    !!!important
        Requires `yaozarrs[io]` or `fsspec` to be installed, unless `obj` is a mapping
        or a [`yaozarrs.ZarrGroup`][] opened from one.

    This is a high-level function to validate both the metadata and the structure
    of a complete OME-Zarr store.  This is the function used by the `yaozarrs validate`
    CLI command.

    Supports OME-Zarr versions 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obj : ZarrGroup | str | Path | Mapping[str, bytes] | Any
        The zarr store to validate. Can be a URI string, a Path, a ZarrGroup instance,
        a zarr.Group object (for backwards compatibility), or a mapping of store keys
        to the bytes of the metadata documents, if you want to do the IO yourself (see
        [`yaozarrs.open_group`][]).  To validate a single document without a store,
        use [`yaozarrs.validate_ome_object`][] or [`yaozarrs.validate_ome_json`][].
    strict : bool | None
        If `True`, reject metadata that would otherwise be coerced to the right type
        (e.g. `"1"` for an integer). By default, such metadata is accepted.

    Returns
    -------
    ZarrGroup
        The opened ZarrGroup if validation is successful.

    Raises
    ------
    StorageValidationError
        If the storage structure is invalid.
    """
    zarr_group = open_group(obj)
    ome_version = zarr_group.ome_version()
    if not ome_version and "ome" in zarr_group.attrs:
        # (OME metadata, so an invalid OME-Zarr group rather than not one at all)
        error = ValidationResult().add_error(
            StorageErrorType.version_missing,
            ("ome", "version"),
            "The OME metadata must declare its 'version'",
        )
        raise StorageValidationError(error.errors)
    if not ome_version:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unable to determine OME-Zarr version for {zarr_group}. "
            "Is this an OME-Zarr group?"
        )

    # (imported here: each version's storage validator imports this module)
    if ome_version == "0.5":
        from .v05._storage import StorageValidatorV05

        Validator = StorageValidatorV05
    elif ome_version == "0.4":
        from .v04._storage import StorageValidatorV04

        Validator = StorageValidatorV04
    elif ome_version in V06_VERSIONS:
        from .v06._storage import StorageValidatorV06

        Validator = StorageValidatorV06
    else:
        error = ValidationResult().add_error(
            StorageErrorType.unsupported_version,
            ("version",),
            f"Unsupported OME-Zarr version {ome_version!r}",
        )
        raise StorageValidationError(error.errors)

    # Capture RuntimeWarnings from pydantic validators during validation
    # and convert them to StorageValidationWarning
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as captured_warnings:
        warnings.filterwarnings("always", category=ValidationWarning)
        result = Validator.validate_group(zarr_group, strict=strict)

    # prepend captured warnings to the result
    for w in captured_warnings:
        details: ErrorDetails = {
            "type": "model_warning",
            "loc": (),
            "msg": str(w.message),
        }
        result.warnings.insert(0, details)

    # Emit warnings for SHOULD directives from structural validation
    if result.warnings:
        # Use a custom formatter to match exception style
        warning_instance = StorageValidationWarning(result.warnings)

        _original_formatwarning = warnings.formatwarning

        def _custom_formatwarning(message, category, *_, **__) -> str:
            # Format like an exception: module.Class: message
            return f"{category.__module__}.{category.__name__}: {message}\n"

        warnings.formatwarning = _custom_formatwarning  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]
        try:
            warnings.warn(warning_instance, stacklevel=2)
        finally:
            warnings.formatwarning = _original_formatwarning

    # Raise error if any validation issues found
    if not result.is_valid:
        raise StorageValidationError(result.errors)

    return zarr_group

Base class for zarr nodes (yaozarrs.ZarrGroup and yaozarrs._zarr.ZarrArray).

This is a minimal implementation that provides access to metadata and hierarchy traversal without requiring a full zarr-python dependency. You cannot read array data directly without depending on zarr-python or tensorstore, but you can navigate the tree and read metadata.

Initialize a zarr node.

Parameters:

The mapping for the zarr store (e.g. an FSMap, or a dict). Anything other than a _CachedMapper will be wrapped in one, for performance.

required path str

The path to this node within the zarr store (relative to the store root).

def __init__(
    self,
    store: Mapping[str, bytes],
    path: str = "",
    meta: ZarrMetadata | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize a zarr node.

    Parameters
    ----------
    store : Mapping[str, bytes]
        The mapping for the zarr store (e.g. an FSMap, or a dict).  Anything other
        than a _CachedMapper will be wrapped in one, for performance.
    path : str
        The path to this node within the zarr store (relative to the store root).
    meta : dict[str, Any] | ZarrMetadata | None
        Optional pre-loaded metadata dictionary. If not provided, it will be
        loaded from the store.
    """
    # Ensure we have a cached mapper for performance
    if not isinstance(store, _CachedMapper):
        store = _CachedMapper(store)

    self._store = store
    self._path = str(path).rstrip("/")
    if meta is None:
        self._metadata = _load_zarr_metadata(self._store, self._path)
    elif isinstance(meta, ZarrMetadata):
        if meta.node_type != self.node_type():  # pragma: no cover
            raise ValueError(
                f"Metadata node_type '{meta.node_type}' does not match "
                f"expected '{self.node_type()}'"
            )
        self._metadata = meta
    else:  # pragma: no cover
        raise ValueError("meta must be a ZarrMetadata instance or None")

Important

Source code in src/yaozarrs/_zarr.py 
def to_zarr_python(self) -> zarr.Array | zarr.Group:
    """Convert to a zarr-python Array or Group object.

    !!!important
        Requires `zarr-python` to be installed.
    """
    try:
        import zarr
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError("zarr package is required for to_zarr_python()") from e

    _mapper, full_path, protocol = self._full_path()
    # zarr's URI parsing doesn't round-trip percent-encoded characters
    # (e.g. spaces), so for local stores hand it the raw path directly.
    target = full_path if protocol in ("file", "local") else self.store_path
    return zarr.open(target, mode="r")

def to_tensorstore(self) -> tensorstore.TensorStore:
    """Convert to a tensorstore TensorStore object.

    !!!important
        Requires `tensorstore` to be installed.
    """
    try:
        import tensorstore as ts
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(
            "tensorstore package is required for to_tensorstore()"
        ) from e

    fsmap, *_ = self._full_path()
    spec = {
        "driver": "zarr3" if self._metadata.zarr_format == 3 else "zarr",
        "kvstore": _fsmap_to_tensorstore_kvstore(fsmap, self._path),
    }
    future = ts.open(spec)
    return future.result()

items.title: Image
items.text:
Top-level OME-NGFF v0.4 image metadata.

This model corresponds to the .zattrs file in an image group (or zarr.json attributes in Zarr v3). It contains one or more multiscale pyramids plus optional OMERO rendering hints.

Typical Structure

my_image/
├── .zattrs            # contains {"multiscales": [...]}
├── 0/                 # Highest resolution array
├── 1/                 # Next resolution level
└── labels/            # Optional segmentation masks

v0.4 vs v0.5

In v0.4, the version field is inside the multiscale objects rather than at the top level. See Multiscale.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default multiscales list[Multiscale]

One or more multiscale image pyramids in this group

required omero Omero | None

Optional OMERO rendering metadata for visualization

None

items.title: Multiscale
items.text:
Multi-resolution image pyramid (<=5D) with coordinate metadata.

Defines an image at one or more resolution levels, along with the coordinate system that relates array indices to physical space. This is the core metadata for any OME-NGFF image.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

Optional identifier for this multiscale image

None axes list[SpaceAxis | TimeAxis | ChannelAxis | CustomAxis]

Ordered list of dimension axes defining the coordinate system

required datasets list[Dataset]

Resolution pyramid levels, from highest to lowest resolution

required coordinateTransformations list[ScaleTransformation | TranslationTransformation] | None

Coordinate transformations that are applied to all resolution levels in the same manner.

None version Literal['0.4'] '0.4' type str | None

Type of downscaling method used to generate the multiscale image pyramid.

None metadata dict | None

Unstructured key-value pair with additional information about the downscaling method.

None

@classmethod
def from_dims(
    cls,
    dims: Sequence[DimSpec],
    name: str | None = None,
    n_levels: int = 1,
) -> Self:
    """Convenience constructor: Create Multiscale from a sequence of DimSpec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dims : Sequence[DimSpec]
        A sequence of dimension specifications defining the image dimensions.
        Must follow OME-Zarr axis ordering: `[time,] [channel,] space...`
    name : str | None, optional
        Name for the multiscale. Default is None.
    n_levels : int, optional
        Number of resolution levels in the pyramid. Default is 1.

    Returns
    -------
    Multiscale
        A fully configured Multiscale model.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v04
    >>> dims = [
    ...     DimSpec(name="t", size=512, unit="second"),
    ...     DimSpec(
    ...         name="z", size=50, scale=2.0, unit="micrometer", scale_factor=1.0
    ...     ),
    ...     DimSpec(name="y", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    ...     DimSpec(name="x", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    ... ]
    >>> ms = v04.Multiscale.from_dims(dims, name="my_multiscale", n_levels=3)
    >>> [ds.path for ds in ms.datasets]
    ['0', '1', '2']
    """
    return cls(name=name, **_axes_datasets(dims, n_levels))  # type: ignore

items.title: Dataset
items.text:
A single resolution level in a multiscale image pyramid.

Each dataset points to a Zarr array and defines how its indices map to physical coordinates. Together, multiple datasets form a resolution pyramid where each level represents the same physical region at different sampling rates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

Path to the Zarr array for this resolution level, relative to the parent multiscale group. All strings are allowed according to the spec, but prefer using only alphanumeric characters, dots (.), underscores (_), or hyphens (-) to avoid issues on some filesystems or when used in URLs.

required coordinateTransformations list[ScaleTransformation | TranslationTransformation]

Transformations mapping array indices to physical coordinates. Must include exactly one scale transformation, and optionally one translation.

required

items.title: ScaleTransformation
items.text:
Maps array indices to physical coordinates via scaling.

Defines the pixel/voxel size in physical units for each dimension. Every dataset must have exactly one scale transformation.

Note

Scale values represent physical size per pixel. For example, a scale of [0.5, 0.5] means each pixel is 0.5 units wide in physical space.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default type Literal['scale'] 'scale' scale list[float]

Scaling factor for each dimension in physical units per pixel

required

Specifies the physical coordinates of the origin (index [0, 0, ...]). At most one translation may be present per dataset, and it must appear after the scale transformation.

items.title: Plate
items.text:
Top-level plate metadata for high-content screening.

This model corresponds to the .zattrs file (or zarr.json attributes) in a plate group, organizing a microplate's wells in a grid layout. Each well contains one or more fields-of-view, which in turn contain multiscale images.

Typical Structure

my_plate.ome.zarr/
├── A/                      # Row A
│   ├── 1/                  # Well A1
│   │   ├── 0/              # FOV 0 in A1
│   │   │   ├── 0/          # Multiscale level 0
│   │   │   └── .zattrs     # contains {"multiscales": [...]}
│   │   ├── 1/              # FOV 1 in A1
│   │   └── .zattrs         # contains {"well": {...}}
│   └── 2/                  # Well A2
├── B/                      # Row B
└── .zattrs                 # contains {"plate": {...}}

Note

See also:

  • Well
  • FieldOfView

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default plate PlateDef

Plate layout and well organization

required bioformats2raw_layout Literal[3] | None

Marker indicating this plate was created by bioformats2raw version 3

None

@classmethod
def from_dims(
    cls,
    dims: Sequence[DimSpec],
    name: str | None = None,
    n_levels: int = 1,
) -> Self:
    """Convenience constructor: Create Multiscale from a sequence of DimSpec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dims : Sequence[DimSpec]
        A sequence of dimension specifications defining the image dimensions.
        Must follow OME-Zarr axis ordering: `[time,] [channel,] space...`
    name : str | None, optional
        Name for the multiscale. Default is None.
    n_levels : int, optional
        Number of resolution levels in the pyramid. Default is 1.

    Returns
    -------
    Multiscale
        A fully configured Multiscale model.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v05
    >>> dims = [
    ...     DimSpec(name="t", size=512, unit="second"),
    ...     DimSpec(
    ...         name="z", size=50, scale=2.0, unit="micrometer", scale_factor=1.0
    ...     ),
    ...     DimSpec(name="y", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    ...     DimSpec(name="x", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    ... ]
    >>> ms = v05.Multiscale.from_dims(dims, name="my_multiscale", n_levels=3)
    >>> [ds.path for ds in ms.datasets]
    ['0', '1', '2']
    """
    return cls(name=name, **_axes_datasets(dims, n_levels))  # type: ignore

items.title: Dataset
items.text:
A single resolution level in a multiscale image pyramid.

Each dataset points to a Zarr array and defines how its indices map to physical coordinates. Together, multiple datasets form a resolution pyramid where each level represents the same physical region at different sampling rates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

Path to the Zarr array for this resolution level, relative to the parent multiscale group. All strings are allowed according to the spec, but prefer using only alphanumeric characters, dots (.), underscores (_), or hyphens (-) to avoid issues on some filesystems or when used in URLs.

required coordinateTransformations list[ScaleTransformation | TranslationTransformation]

Transformations mapping array indices to physical coordinates. Must include exactly one scale transformation, and optionally one translation.

required

Return the scale transformation from the list.

(CoordinateTransformsList validator ensures there is exactly one.)

Return the translation transformation from the list, if present.

(CoordinateTransformsList validator ensures there is at most one.)

items.title: ScaleTransformation
items.text:
Maps array indices to physical coordinates via scaling.

Defines the pixel/voxel size in physical units for each dimension. Every dataset must have exactly one scale transformation.

Note

Scale values represent physical size per pixel. For example, a scale of [0.5, 0.5] means each pixel is 0.5 units wide in physical space.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default type Literal['scale'] 'scale' scale list[float]

Scaling factor for each dimension in physical units per pixel

required

items.title: TranslationTransformation
items.text:
Translates the coordinate system origin in physical space.

Specifies the physical coordinates of the origin (index [0, 0, ...]). At most one translation may be present per dataset, and it must appear after the scale transformation.

required

items.title: Bf2Raw
items.text:
Model for zarr.json in a group representing multi-series image collections.

The bioformats2raw layout was added in v0.4 as a transitional specification to specify filesets that already exist in the wild. An upcoming NGFF specification will replace this layout with explicit metadata.

This model is a transitional spec for representing multi-position image collections in OME-NGFF v0.5. It is currently the only way to represent multi-position image collections. It also has a recommended place for OME-XML metadata.

Typical Structure

root.ome.zarr             # One converted fileset from bioformats2raw
├── zarr.json             # Contains "bioformats2raw.layout" metadata
├── OME                   # Special group for containing OME metadata
│   ├── zarr.json         # Contains "series" metadata
│   └── METADATA.ome.xml  # OME-XML file stored within the Zarr fileset
├── 0                     # First image in the collection
├── 1                     # Second image in the collection
└── ...

Note

The OME/zarr.json file typically contains Series metadata that explicitly lists image paths. If not present, images MUST be numbered as shown above, starting from 0, e.g., 0/, 1/, 2/, etc.

├── 0                     # First image in the collection
├── 1                     # Second image in the collection
└── ...

@classmethod
def from_dims(
    cls,
    dims: Sequence[DimSpec],
    name: str | None = None,
    n_levels: int = 1,
    coordinate_system: str = "intrinsic",
) -> Self:
    """Convenience constructor: Create Multiscale from a sequence of DimSpec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dims : Sequence[DimSpec]
        A sequence of dimension specifications defining the image dimensions.
        Must follow OME-Zarr axis ordering: `[time,] [channel,] space...`
    name : str | None, optional
        Name for the multiscale. Default is None.
    n_levels : int, optional
        Number of resolution levels in the pyramid. Default is 1.
    coordinate_system : str, optional
        Name of the (intrinsic) coordinate system that all resolution levels map
        into. Default is "intrinsic".

    Returns
    -------
    Multiscale
        A fully configured Multiscale model.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from yaozarrs import DimSpec, v06
    >>> dims = [
    ...     DimSpec(name="t", size=512, unit="second"),
    ...     DimSpec(
    ...         name="z", size=50, scale=2.0, unit="micrometer", scale_factor=1.0
    ...     ),
    ...     DimSpec(name="y", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),
    ...     DimSpec(name="x", size=512, scale=0.5, unit="micrometer"),

    >>> ms = v06.Multiscale.from_dims(dims, name="my_multiscale", n_levels=3)
    >>> [ds.path for ds in ms.datasets]
    ['0', '1', '2']
    """
    layout = _coordinate_systems_datasets(dims, n_levels, coordinate_system)
    return cls.model_validate({"name": name, **layout})

items.title: validate_multiscale_axes
items.text:
validate_multiscale_axes(axes: Sequence[Axis]) -> None

Rules for the axes of coordinate systems inside multiscales metadata.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the axes violate any of the rules.

Source code in src/yaozarrs/v06/_axes.py 
def validate_multiscale_axes(axes: Sequence[Axis]) -> None:
    """Rules for the axes of coordinate systems inside `multiscales` metadata.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the axes violate any of the rules.
    """
    # NOTE: the prose says these rules "apply to all coordinate systems inside
    # multiscales metadata", including "`axes` MUST contain 2 or 3 entries of
    # `type:space`".  But axes.schema allows either 2-3 "space" axes or >= 2 "array"
    # axes, so we accept the latter with a warning.
    # (only the space-axis rule is relaxed for those; the other rules still apply)
    n_space = sum(ax.type == "space" for ax in axes)
    array_cs = sum(ax.type == "array" for ax in axes) >= 2 and not 2 <= n_space <= 3
    if array_cs:
        warnings.warn(
            "Coordinate systems inside multiscales MUST contain 2 or 3 axes of type "
            "'space' according to the spec prose; coordinate systems made of 'array' "
            "axes are only allowed by the JSON schema.",
            ValidationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    # The length of `axes` must be between 2 and 5
    if not 2 <= len(axes) <= 5:
        raise ValueError(f"There must be between 2 and 5 axes. Found {len(axes)}.")

    # `axes` MUST contain 2 or 3 entries of `type:space`
    if not array_cs and not 2 <= n_space <= 3:
        raise ValueError("There must be 2 or 3 axes of type 'space'.")
    # `axes` MAY contain one additional entry of `type:time`
    if sum(ax.type == "time" for ax in axes) > 1:
        raise ValueError("There can be at most 1 axis of type 'time'.")
    # `axes` MAY contain one additional entry of `type:channel` or a null / custom type.
    # NOTE: this sentence is unchanged from v0.5; like v05 we only limit `channel` axes
    # to one, and allow several custom/untyped axes (within the 5-axis limit).
    if sum(ax.type == "channel" for ax in axes) > 1:
        raise ValueError("There can be at most 1 axis of type 'channel'.")

    # `axes` entries MUST be ordered by `type` where the `time` axis must come first
    # (if present), followed by the `channel` or custom axis (if present) and the
    # axes of type `space`.
    type_order = {"time": 0, "space": 2}
    order = [type_order.get(ax.type or "", 1) for ax in axes]
    if order != sorted(order):
        raise ValueError(
            "Axes are not in the required order by type. "
            "Order must be [time,] [channel or custom,] space."
        )

items.title: check_transform_ndim
items.text:
check_transform_ndim(
    t: CoordinateTransformation, n_in: int, n_out: int
) -> None

Check that the parameters of t fit n_in input and n_out output axes.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If they don't.

Source code in src/yaozarrs/v06/_transforms.py 
def check_transform_ndim(t: CoordinateTransformation, n_in: int, n_out: int) -> None:
    """Check that the parameters of `t` fit `n_in` input and `n_out` output axes.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If they don't.
    """

    # The parameter values ... MUST be compatible with input and output space
    # dimensionality
    def _fail(msg: str) -> NoReturn:
        raise ValueError(f"{t.type}: {msg} (input has {n_in}, output has {n_out} axes)")

    if isinstance(t, (TranslationTransformation, ScaleTransformation)):
        # Input and output dimensionality MUST be identical and MUST equal the
        # length of the `scale`/`translation` array (N).
        params = t.translation if isinstance(t, TranslationTransformation) else t.scale
        if not len(params) == n_in == n_out:
            _fail(f"has {len(params)} values")
    elif isinstance(t, (IdentityTransformation, DisplacementsTransformation)):
        # (`displacements` require M=N)
        if n_in != n_out:
            _fail("input and output must have the same number of axes")
    elif isinstance(t, MapAxisTransformation):
        # The length of the array MUST equal the number of dimensions in both the
        # input and output coordinate systems. Each integer in the array MUST be a
        # valid zero-based index into the input coordinate system's axes
        # (that it's a permutation of 0..N-1 is checked by MapAxisTransformation)
        if not len(t.mapAxis) == n_in == n_out:
            _fail(f"has {len(t.mapAxis)} indices")
    elif isinstance(t, ProjectAxisTransformation):
        dropped, created = t.droppedInputs or [], t.createdOutputs or []
        if any(i >= n_in for i in dropped):
            _fail(f"droppedInputs {dropped} out of range")
        if any(i >= n_out for i in created):
            _fail(f"createdOutputs {created} out of range")
        if n_out != n_in - len(dropped) + len(created):
            _fail(f"drops {len(dropped)} and creates {len(created)} axes")
    elif isinstance(t, AffineTransformation):
        # the outer array MUST be length `M` and the inner arrays MUST be length N+1
        if t.affine is not None:
            m, n1 = len(t.affine), len(t.affine[0])
            if m != n_out or n1 != n_in + 1:
                _fail(f"matrix is {m}x{n1}, expected {n_out}x{n_in + 1}")
    elif isinstance(t, RotationTransformation):
        # Input and output dimensionality (N) MUST be identical.
        if n_in != n_out:
            _fail("input and output must have the same number of axes")
        if t.rotation is not None and len(t.rotation) != n_in:
            _fail(f"matrix is {len(t.rotation)}x{len(t.rotation)}")
    elif isinstance(t, BijectionTransformation):
        # Its input and output spaces MUST have equal dimension. The input and
        # output dimensions for the both the forward and inverse transformations
        # MUST match bijection's input and output space dimensions.
        if n_in != n_out:
            _fail("input and output must have the same number of axes")
        _check_child(t, "forward", t.forward, n_in, n_out)
        _check_child(t, "inverse", t.inverse, n_out, n_in)
    elif isinstance(t, SequenceTransformation):
        # (intermediate dimensionality is inferred from each step's parameters. Where
        # it can't be (e.g. after a `coordinates` step), checking resumes at the next
        # step whose parameters fix its own input size. The last step must produce
        # the sequence's output.)
        n: int | None = n_in
        steps = t.transformations
        for i, step in enumerate(steps):
            if n is None:
                n = _own_ndim(step)[0]
            n_next = n_out if i == len(steps) - 1 else _output_ndim(step, n)
            if n is not None and n_next is not None:
                _check_child(t, f"transformations[{i}]", step, n, n_next)
            n = n_next
    elif isinstance(t, ByDimensionTransformation):
        # The integer values in these arrays correspond to the axis indices in the
        # `byDimension`'s ... `input` and `output` coordinate systems
        for i, item in enumerate(t.transformations):
            if any(ax >= n_in for ax in item.inputAxes):
                _fail(f"transformations[{i}].inputAxes {item.inputAxes} out of range")
            if any(ax >= n_out for ax in item.outputAxes):
                _fail(f"transformations[{i}].outputAxes {item.outputAxes} out of range")
        # Every axis index in the parent byDimension's `output` coordinate system
        # MUST appear in exactly one child transformation's `outputAxes` array.
        covered = {ax for item in t.transformations for ax in item.outputAxes}
        if missing := sorted(set(range(n_out)) - covered):
            _fail(f"output axes {missing} are not covered by any transformation")

items.title: Bf2Raw
items.text:
Model for zarr.json in a group representing multi-series image collections.

The bioformats2raw layout is a transitional specification for filesets that already exist in the wild. An upcoming NGFF specification will replace this layout with explicit metadata. It is currently the only way to represent multi-position image collections, and it has a recommended place for OME-XML metadata.

Typical Structure

root.ome.zarr             # One converted fileset from bioformats2raw
├── zarr.json             # Contains "bioformats2raw.layout" metadata
├── OME                   # Special group for containing OME metadata
│   ├── zarr.json         # Contains "series" metadata
│   └── METADATA.ome.xml  # OME-XML file stored within the Zarr fileset
├── 0                     # First image in the collection
├── 1                     # Second image in the collection
└── ...

Note

The OME/zarr.json file typically contains Series metadata that explicitly lists image paths. If not present, images MUST be numbered as shown above, starting from 0, e.g., 0/, 1/, 2/, etc.
